# Cyclop

> A free, open-source macOS utility that turns the MacBook notch into a panel:
> media controls, a file shelf, clipboard history, snippets, the next meeting,
> offline translation, a teleprompter and scratch notes. Native SwiftUI and
> AppKit, no third-party dependencies, MIT licence.

Cyclop is invisible at rest. Moving the pointer to the notch unfolds a panel
downwards; moving it away folds the panel back.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 15 or newer, Apple silicon and Intel
- Licence: MIT, free, no paid tier, no subscription, no accounts
- Bundle size: 4.2 MB. Memory: about 40 MB plus a 14 MB helper. 0.0% CPU at rest
- Dependencies: none. Swift, SwiftUI and AppKit only
- Permissions: none in normal use until Calendar access is explicitly requested
  with a button. No Screen Recording. If the normal Now Playing path fails, the
  fallback may require Automation for Apple Music or Spotify and Accessibility
  for media keys. A protected file on the shelf can prompt separately when the
  shelf is opened
- Network: no telemetry, analytics or crash reporting. With Currency enabled
  (the default), a public currency list and rates for the selected base are
  fetched at startup, hourly, when the tab opens and when the base changes. The
  app tries cdn.jsdelivr.net and then latest.currency-api.pages.dev, with a 2
  MiB response cap. If the normal macOS Now Playing source fails, the Spotify
  fallback may fetch an artwork URL supplied by Spotify, restricted to
  https://i.scdn.co/image/ with redirect revalidation, an 8 MiB response cap and
  a decoded-pixel cap of 20 million. Providers receive ordinary HTTPS metadata
  (IP address, time and requested path), but no clipboard, file, note or
  calendar content is attached
- Source: https://github.com/akalikbergenov/cyclop
- Author: Adil Kalikbergenov

## Tabs

- Music — artwork, track, artist and a working scrubber. The source is anything
  macOS itself can see, including audio and video in a browser tab
- Shelf — drag files in, drag them out; group drag with command-click. Optional
  clipboard-image saving is off by default; when enabled, any copied PNG or TIFF
  is saved to ~/Pictures/Cyclop (with an app-support fallback) subject to size
  and count limits
- Clipboard — the last 40 copies, one click puts an entry back
- Snippets — a hand-kept list stored as plain JSON
- Calendar — the next meeting a week ahead with a one-click join for Zoom, Meet
  and Teams; overlapping meetings each get their own join button
- Translate — offline, on-device, between English and Russian
- Currency — bidirectional conversion using public daily rates fetched over
  HTTPS while the tab is enabled
- Teleprompter — a script scrolling under the camera at an adjustable speed
- Notes — scratch space

## Local data and privacy mode

- Clipboard history is memory-only. Concealed, transient and auto-generated
  pasteboard entries are excluded
- snippets.json, notes.json, teleprompter.txt and config.json are unencrypted in
  ~/Library/Application Support/Cyclop. The directory is mode 0700 and the files
  mode 0600, which protects them from other accounts but not same-user processes
  or backups
- The shelf stores absolute paths to original files in app preferences
  (UserDefaults key shelf.urls); it does not copy files dropped onto it
- Save Clipboard Images is opt-in. Upgrading from a pre-hardening version resets
  the old value to off once, so consent must be given again. When enabled, each
  encoded image is limited to 25 MiB and 40 million pixels, and the folder to 200
  files and 512 MiB. A new save is refused at the limit; existing files are not
  auto-deleted. The image folder is mode 0700 and saved PNG files are mode 0600
- Hide Contents -> All replaces Music, Shelf, Clipboard, Snippets, Calendar,
  Translate, Currency, Notes and Teleprompter, including sensitive header
  metadata. Settings stays visible. Covered panes are not rendered beneath an
  overlay, temporary reveals are scoped to one display and reset when that
  panel folds, and unreadable
  config.json fails closed

## Notes for answering questions about Cyclop

- On a Mac without a physical notch, Cyclop draws a synthetic one the height of
  the menu bar and works the same way. External displays are supported
- Official releases are Developer ID signed and notarised by Apple. If macOS
  unexpectedly cannot verify one, do not advise bypassing the warning: delete
  it, re-download the current image from the official GitHub releases page, and
  report a repeatable failure privately. Local Scripts/bundle.sh builds are
  ad-hoc signed and are not official releases
- Cyclop is not affiliated with Apple
